new_issues.description: Appendix B's perception-noise parameter changed from 'standard deviation between 0.06 and 0.12 by dimension' (round 4) to '0.06 on every dimension', while no case-study number in numbers.tex changed between versions. The same model is therefore documented with two different noise specifications across rounds, and the manuscript does not say which is correct. If the new value is wrong, the specification contradicts the model behind the reported numbers.
new_issues.location_anchor: text: App.B Submodels, 'the noise $\eta$ is Gaussian with standard deviation 0.06 on every dimension'
new_issues.competence_basis: Line-by-line comparison of App.B in the original and revised main.tex, and of numbers.tex (no case macros changed).
new_issues.attribution_evidence: Changed in this revision (diff of App.B Submodels). The manuscript inputs cannot show whether the old or the new value matches the code, so this is either a correction or a regression.
new_issues.non_match_rationale: R2 asks that the missing parameters be stated; it does not cover the accuracy of a parameter changed between versions without explanation.

new_issues.description: Appendix B process step (6) still defines the perceived policy as '$\tau_i(p + b_i) + \eta$ shrunk toward its trust target'. That reads as shrinking twice, with the noise inside the shrinkage. The new Submodels formula $a_i + \tau_i(p+b_i-a_i)+\eta$ shrinks once, with the noise outside. The two descriptions of the same step disagree.
new_issues.location_anchor: text: App.B Process overview step (6), '$\tau_i(p + b_i) + \eta$ shrunk toward its trust target'
new_issues.competence_basis: Algebraic comparison of the two expressions in App.B.
new_issues.attribution_evidence: The explicit formula is new in this revision (diff of App.B Submodels). Step (6) was left unchanged, so the revision introduced the inconsistency.
new_issues.non_match_rationale: R2 required a general perception formula, which is now given; the conflict with an unchanged sentence elsewhere in App.B is a separate consistency defect.
